# Results — Study 316 (Bank-Failure) on the real daily tape

*Generated by the event-study engine in [`bank_failure/strategy.py`](../bank_failure/strategy.py).
An event study of SPY (and the financials sector ETF XLF) around a hardcoded table of
headline bank-failure / forced-rescue dates — the day each failure was **public knowledge**
(announcement / FDIC seizure / forced sale), so the window is anchored there with no extra
lag. Closes are Yahoo! adjusted (auto_adjust=True — total-return-ish, **not** price-only).
As-of **2026-06-18**; match the per-tape fingerprint to confirm you hold the same tape.*

## Data stamp

| Ticker | Window | Days | Fingerprint |

| SPY | 1993-01-29 → 2026-06-18 | 8,404 | `c3d89ac3d3f5` |
| XLF | 1998-12-22 → 2026-06-18 | 6,914 | `78429d2d69ba` |

## The event table (12 failures; 11 fit SPY's window — 1984 Continental Illinois predates SPY)

Continental Illinois (1984), Northern Rock (2007), Bear Stearns (2008-03), IndyMac
(2008-07), **Lehman (2008-09-15)**, WaMu (2008-09-25), Wachovia (2008-09-29), MF Global
(2011), **SVB (2023-03-10)**, Signature (2023-03-12), **Credit Suisse (2023-03-19)**,
First Republic (2023-05-01).

## The headline — SPY, day-0 close anchor, +20 trading days, adjusted

| Horizon | n | mean CAR | median CAR | win-rate | HAC/plain *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Event day (day 0) | 11 | **−1.53%** | — | — | — |
| +5 trading days | 11 | −1.35% | −0.02% | 45% | −0.71 |
| **+20 trading days** | 11 | **−5.50%** | **+3.20%** | **64%** | **−0.93** |
| +60 trading days | 11 | −5.8% | — | — | −0.77 |

- The mean +20d move is a scary **−5.50%** — but the **median is +3.20%** and 64% of
  events were *up* after 20 days. The mean is dragged underwater by a handful of
  catastrophes, not by a systematic post-failure decline.
- The HAC/plain *t* is **−0.93** (n=11). **Far below the inference bar (|t| ≥ 2).** A
  block-bootstrap 95% CI on the +20d mean spans **[−17.3%, +3.9%]** — it comfortably
  contains zero (and large positive numbers). On the tape, "bank failure ⇒ market move"
  is **statistically indistinguishable from noise**.

## It's not a signal — it's the 2008 cluster (the misattribution)

| Subset | n | mean +20d | median +20d |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **2008 cluster** (Lehman, WaMu, Wachovia, Bear, IndyMac) | 5 | **−15.5%** | — |
| **2023 cluster** (SVB, Signature, Credit Suisse, First Republic) | 4 | **+4.6%** | — |
| **Everything except 2008** | 6 | **+2.8%** | **+5.1%** |

Per-event SPY +20d CAR makes the story unmissable:

| Event | +20d CAR |
|---|--:|
| Northern Rock 2007 | +5.3% |
| Bear Stearns 2008-03 | +3.3% |
| IndyMac 2008-07 | +3.2% |
| **Lehman 2008-09** | **−21.3%** |
| **WaMu 2008-09** | **−26.0%** |
| **Wachovia 2008-09** | **−36.4%** |
| MF Global 2011 | −6.9% |
| SVB 2023-03 | +4.9% |
| Signature 2023-03 | +6.4% |
| Credit Suisse 2023-03 | +6.0% |
| First Republic 2023-05 | +1.0% |

Drop the single worst event (Wachovia) and the mean already halves to −2.4%. Strip the
whole **2008** cluster and the remaining six failures averaged **+2.8%** (median **+5.1%**,
*t* = +1.34) — i.e. on average the market *bounced*. **The "warning" is not "a bank
failed"; it is "it was the autumn of 2008."** The 2023 mini-crisis — three banks down in
ten days, including a 167-year-old G-SIB — was a clean +4.6% rebound.

## Why the placebo p-value is a trap (the confound, stated honestly)

A naive permutation test (event mean CAR vs 3,000 random-date placebos) returns a
"significant" result — SPY event mean −5.5% vs placebo mean +0.8%, **z = −4.5, p < 0.001**;
XLF z = −4.6. **We do not stamp on this.** The events cluster inside one bear market, so a
random-date placebo is really asking *"were these dates in 2008?"*, not *"is a bank failure
a signal?"* — the synthetic/placebo control is a **machinery proof** (it confirms the
engine detects a planted drift — see the positive control), never market evidence for a
stamp. Under the desk's inference bar, the per-event HAC *t* is the number that decides,
and it is **−0.93**.

## XLF (financials sector) — same shape, same non-result

| Horizon | n | mean CAR | win-rate | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| +20 trading days | 11 | **−9.11%** | 36% | −1.24 |
| +20d, ex-2008 | 6 | −1.7% (median −2.3%) | — | — |

Financials fall harder on the day and over 20 days (it is their own sector blowing up),
but the *t* is still below 2, and ex-2008 the move is a modest −1.7%. Even the directly
afflicted sector carries no certifiable post-failure signal once the 2008 cluster is set
aside.

## Could you trade it? — the "buy the blood" overlay (SPY, +20d hold)

| One-way cost | net mean / trade | win-rate | *t* | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 bps (gross) | **−2.79%** | 67% | −0.62 | 12 |
| 5 bps | −2.89% | 67% | −0.65 | 12 |
| 10 bps | −2.99% | 67% | −0.67 | 12 |

The overlay **loses money before any cost** (−2.79%/trade gross). Costs are charged
one-way × NAV on both legs and barely matter — the gross is already negative. A 67%
win-rate alongside a −2.79% mean is the familiar win-rate-vs-expectancy gap: many small
rebounds, a few catastrophic 2008 trades. There is nothing to scale, with or without
costs.

## Robustness — a conservative next-close fill

Anchoring entry one trading day later (`lag=1`) leaves the picture unchanged (event mean
−3.0%, still dominated by 2008). The result is not a same-day-close artefact; it is a
small-sample, one-cluster non-result either way.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is a faithful detector

On a deterministic synthetic tape with a *planted* post-event drift, the same engine
recovers the effect **only when it is real**, and calls the null a null:

| Planted post-event drift | event CAR vs placebo | permutation p | detected? |
|---|--:|--:|:--:|
| 0.00 (pure null) | ≈ placebo | > 0.05 | no (correct) |
| +0.08 (rebound) | well above placebo | < 0.05 (z > 2) | yes |

The harness can bank a planted signal and ignores a null — so the real-tape non-result is
a statement about *the market* (too few, too clustered to certify anything), not a broken
pipeline.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** SPY +20d mean CAR −5.50% but HAC/plain *t* = −0.93 (n=11), 95% CI
  [−17.3%, +3.9%], median *positive* (+3.2%). Indistinguishable from noise; the scary
  mean is one cluster, not a signal.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The "buy the blood" overlay loses −2.79%/trade gross before a
  cent of cost; nothing to scale.
- **A reliable warning? — MISATTRIBUTED.** The bearish average is the autumn-2008 cluster
  (−15.5%); strip it and the other six failures averaged +2.8% (median +5.1%), and the
  2023 crisis bounced +4.6%. "Bank failure" is a label pasted onto "it was 2008."
